models.name: rf_robust
models.label: Random Forest — Sensor-robust (deployed)
models.conditions: Deployed. Rank within property type (flats 0.8642 vs 0.9047); pair with CO2 sensor repair; surface a reliability flag; re-audit after one heating season.
models.narrative: Random Forest — Sensor-robust (deployed) — missingness: CO2 dropped. AUROC 0.9129, sensitivity 0.8874, PPV 0.6378 at threshold 0.43 (5-fold property-level CV, n=250). Flats AUROC 0.8642 vs terraced 0.9047. Deployed model — non-linear, best accuracy and the fairest across property types (flats 0.8642). CONDITIONAL: small residual flat gap to monitor; rank within type.

deployment_questions.q1: At threshold 0.43 sensitivity is 0.8874; misses ~11.3% of cold property-days (6078 of 53982 in held-out CV).
deployment_questions.q2: PPV 0.6378 — a positive flag is right ~64% of the time.
deployment_questions.q3: NPV 0.9435 — an all-clear is right ~94% of the time.
deployment_questions.q4: AUROC 0.9129 — ranks a cold property above a warm one ~91% of the time.
deployment_questions.q5: Per-type AUROC flat 0.8642 / terraced 0.9047 / semi 0.903 / detached 0.8936. Flats weakest — rank within type.
deployment_questions.q6: Uses no CO2, so the 38% MNAR dropout cannot affect it; the broken sensors are flagged for repair separately.
deployment_questions.q7: A false negative leaves a genuinely cold household below 19C for another heating season — a delayed health outcome for vulnerable residents.
deployment_questions.q8: Yes — primary ranking engine, with per-type ranking and a sensor-repair workstream.

models.label: Gradient Boosting — CO2 (native NaN)
models.conditions: Strong alternative; CO2 adds no benefit, so prefer the simpler CO2-free forest unless native missing-handling is specifically required.

overall_notes: CONDITIONAL. Temperature/humidity/smart-meter reliable; CO2 MNAR (38% missing, 40 properties >=50% dropout) but uninformative — adding CO2 lifts AUROC by at most +0.003 within a fixed model, and a gradient model handling CO2 natively only matches the CO2-free model. Property-level split verified (0 overlap); lag_temp excluded as target leakage. Deploy the sensor-robust Random Forest (AUROC 0.9129, flats 0.8642); the logistic baseline was unfair to flats (0.6784). Rank within type; repair CO2 sensors; re-audit after one season.

option_specific.title: Cold-Home Triage — coverage + sensor-health + fairness + missingness (4-in-1)

content.reranking_under_fair_weighting: A single cold-risk list ranks houses above flats because flats are genuinely warmer (10.5% vs ~37% cold). Within-type allocation adds 14 flats the global top 50 omits. Choose 'coldest absolute' vs 'coldest per type' deliberately.

threshold_sensitivity_report.sensitivity_fatigue_tradeoff: At 0.5 dropout cut-off, 40 properties flagged for repair — the natural break (MNAR cohort at 70-95%). 0.3 flags 140 (fatigue); 0.8 flags 24 (misses borderline failures).

fairness_disparity_summary.recommended_mitigation: Flag-rate gaps mirror true cold differences, not unfairness. The real risk is lower reliability for flats (AUROC 0.8642). Mitigate with per-type ranking, a UI reliability flag, and CO2 sensor repair.

mechanism.mechanism_verdict: Dropout is only weakly tied to property type.
mechanism.outcome_note: Dropout is only weakly correlated with cold-risk (r=0.0366), so the MNAR-with-respect-to-outcome concern is limited: the broken sensors are mainly a data-integrity issue, not a hidden cold-risk bias.

missingness_analysis.distribution_note: Observed CO2 std is 63.5; naive mean-imputation drops it to 49.8 (a fake spike at the mean), while per-property interpolation keeps it at 58.5 — closer to reality.
